rows.note: This is the all-purpose Cantonese pattern for saying that each of two people or things has the stated property or performs the stated action.

example.jyutping: loeng5 go3 fong1 on3 dou1 ho2 hang4

rows.note: Use this when the two individuals or items are named explicitly rather than referred to as a pair.

example.english: Both Ming and Fong like drinking tea.
example.traditional: 阿明同阿芳都鍾意飲茶。
example.jyutping: aa3 ming4 tung4 aa3 fong1 dou1 zung1 ji3 jam2 caa4

rows.note: Use this mainly in formal or written contexts for two previously mentioned alternatives or entities.

example.jyutping: loeng5 ze2 dou1 gok3 jau5 jau1 dim2

rows.note: Use 兩個都 as the all-purpose choice for two people or countable items.

example.english: Both of these people can speak Cantonese.
example.traditional: 呢兩個人兩個都識講廣東話。
example.jyutping: ni1 loeng5 go3 jan4 loeng5 go3 dou1 sik1 gong2 gwong2 dung1 waa2

rows.note: Use 兩樣都 when the two things are types, varieties, or uncountable alternatives rather than two countable objects.

example.english: Both black tea and green tea can be served iced.
example.traditional: 紅茶同綠茶兩樣都可以凍飲。
example.jyutping: hung4 caa4 tung4 luk6 caa4 loeng5 joeng6 dou1 ho2 ji5 dung3 jam2
